subject: Chemistry
q: What is formed when gypsum is heated to 393 K?
hint: At this temperature gypsum loses only part of its water of crystallization.
solution: Gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O. On heating to about 393 K, it loses 1.5 molecules of water per formula unit: CaSO₄·2H₂O → CaSO₄·0.5H₂O + 1.5H₂O. The calcium sulphate hemihydrate formed is plaster of Paris. Complete dehydration to dead-burnt plaster requires stronger heating.
